blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) answers questions by retrieving over a knowledge graph built from a corpus. Yet retrieval strategies are designed around the structure their own construction pipeline produces, and whether they survive a change of construction is rarely tested. We study this cross-construction portability: whether one retrieval procedure, with no construction-specific schema, relation names, or retuning, stays effective when the graph is built differently. We introduce ArcRAG, which induces a query-local graph interface at inference time (the node labels, relation descriptors, and property keys reachable from the entities a question names), plans multi-hop traversals against it, and executes and repairs them as Cypher. We build each of the MuSiQue, HotpotQA, and TriviaQA corpora as a schema-guided graph (typed nodes, a closed relation set, source provenance) and as an open-information-extraction graph (untyped nodes, free-text relations), with the retriever's configuration fixed across them. We compare against a construction-agnostic Direct-Cypher agent, ablate each stage across retry and pass budgets on both graph families, and compare with results reported for prior GraphRAG systems, most of which design retrieval together with their own graph construction. Across the two constructions, we find that retrieval need not be co-designed with the graph: query-time interface induction keeps a construction-agnostic retriever effective when the construction changes, although construction still shapes absolute accuracy.
blocks.zh: 基于图形的检索增强生成(GraphRAG)通过对从一个实体中构建的知识图进行检索来回答问题. 然而,回收战略是围绕着它们自己生产的建筑管道的结构设计的,它们是否在建筑改变后幸存下来很少经过测试。 我们研究了这种跨构造的可移植性:当图形的构建不同时,一个没有特定构造方案、关系名称或重新调整的检索程序是否仍然有效。 我们引入了ArcRAG,它诱导了一个在推论时间的查询-局部图界面(节点标签,关系描述符,以及实体可以到达的属性密钥一个问号),计划了多跳转对它,并作为Cypher执行和修复. 我们把MusiQue,HotpotQA,TriviaQA corpora 的每个图建成一个以图示为指南的图集(型号为节点,闭合关系集,源代码为源代码),并作为开放信息采集图集(非型号为节点,自由文本关系),其间固定了检索器的配置. 我们比较了一种构造不可知的直线-线圈剂,通过两个图系的重试和通过预算来降低每个阶段,并与以往的GraphRAG系统报告的结果进行比较,这些系统大多是设计检索和自己的图构造。 在整个两个构造中,我们发现检索不需要与图表共同设计:查询-时间界面感应在构造改变时保持一个构造-不可知的检索器有效,尽管构造仍然塑造绝对的准确性.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds a language model in an external
corpus by retrieving information pieces (passages) most similar to a query and conditioning
generation on them. Similarity ranking is sufficient when the answer is
contained in a single passage, and insufficient when the answer must be
composed across several. Consider a question of the form which member
of a given film’s cast has two children who attended a particular
university : answering it requires enumerating a set, testing a property of
each of its elements, and verifying a constraint that no individual passage
asserts. Top- k k alone cannot perform these operations. Graph-based RAG
addresses this by retrieving over a knowledge graph (KG) rather than a flat
collection of passages, so that the relations connecting evidence are part of
what retrieval returns. Composition, though, is only half of what these
settings demand: in regulated domains — finance, law, healthcare,
compliance — questions are seldom one-hop, and an answer must also be traceable to the specific disclosure, clause, or record it rests on. Success in these
settings is evidence returned together with the path that connects it,
rather than the k k passages nearest a query.

blocks.en:
Dense embedding retrieval, the workhorse of naive RAG, cannot supply that,
and the reason is structural rather than a matter of scale. Each passage is
represented independently, while a multi-hop question depends on the
relations among passages. As corpora grow and reasoning chains
lengthen, the relevant facts remain individually retrievable yet become relationally invisible : a vector index surfaces the constituent
pieces without representing the path that joins them, leaving the generator
to reconstruct those connections from semantically similar text amid
substantial surrounding noise. FinReflectKG–MultiHop demonstrates that this
is not a deficiency stronger models will absorb: even reasoning-oriented
models perform better given precisely KG-linked evidence than given
text-only page windows that contain the same facts in less structured
context ( Arun et al., 2025b ) . Knowledge graphs close this
representational gap directly. Typed edges turn “which entity connects to
which” into a traversable structure, and the traversal followed during
retrieval can itself serve as provenance. This is the insight behind
GraphRAG ( Edge et al., 2025 ) and the class of graph-based retrieval
systems it inspired, and it reduces the open problem to a single question:
given a knowledge graph, how should one retrieve over it?

blocks.en:
The difficulty in answering that question is that a knowledge graph is not
one kind of object. Graphs differ in schema commitment , from open
information extraction with free-text relation strings to schema-guided
extraction against a closed, typed relation set, and in whether edges carry provenance back to a source chunk. Most GraphRAG systems fix one point
in this space and design retrieval for it, and cross-construction
portability is rarely tested directly.

Instead, each fixes a point in that space and builds a strategy that
presupposes it. Personalized PageRank presupposes a dense synonymy-linked
entity graph, and returns a ranked passage list rather than a traversal a user
can cite ( Gutiérrez et al., 2025a ) ; GraphRAG’s global search presupposes a hierarchical
Leiden partition and the community summaries precomputed over it ( Edge et al., 2025 ) ; LightRAG’s dual-level retrieval presupposes an
entity-and-relation keyword index and remains a one-hop lookup ( Guo et al., 2025 ) ; and PathRAG selects paths
by a heuristic computed once over a precomputed path index, with no mechanism
for noticing a wrong turn ( Chen et al., 2025 ) .
Agentic methods loosen the fixed strategy but not the coupling: LLM-guided
traversal over graphs ( Sun et al., 2024 ; Luo et al., 2024 ; Jiang et al., 2023 ; Jin et al., 2024 ) proceeds against node and edge semantics known in advance, and the BYOKG line ( Mavromatis et al., 2025 ; Agarwal et al., 2024a ) queries unfamiliar graphs but
pairs exploration with a per-graph preparation or linking stage rather than
deriving the semantics at query time (§ 2 ).

blocks.en:
What these strategies share is not a common weakness but a common coupling:
because each encodes assumptions about the graph it runs on, retrieval and
construction cannot be varied independently. Agentic methods that let a language
model walk a graph directly ( Sun et al., 2024 ; Luo et al., 2024 ; Jiang et al., 2023 ; Jin et al., 2024 ) loosen the fixed-strategy assumption but not the coupling: they traverse
using node and edge semantics supplied in advance, most often those of a
curated graph with a fixed ontology (§ 2 ). The strategy we
describe is specified independently of construction: one retrieval procedure,
applied unchanged to graphs that differ in edge semantics and connectivity.

blocks.en:
ArcRAG separates graph retrieval into exploration and exploitation. It reads each graph’s schema by introspection, which says how
the graph is stored, and an Explorer queries the graph at inference
time for a query-local graph interface : the relation descriptors and
paths reachable from the entities the question names. Exploration is also prompted to surface aliases and paraphrased relation
descriptors near those entities, so later stages work over the variants a
noisy graph contains without an offline canonicalization pass. A Planner and a Generator then exploit what was found, choosing paths and executing
them as Cypher, and the search returns to exploration when the evidence
falls short. No step requires graph-specific prompts, relation names, or
retuning (§ 4 ).

blocks.en:
GraphRAG ( Edge et al., 2025 ) precomputes community summaries over a
hierarchical partition; HippoRAG ( Gutiérrez et al., 2025a ) runs personalized PageRank
over an OpenIE graph, and HippoRAG 2 ( Gutiérrez et al., 2025b ) adds denser phrase and
passage indexing; LightRAG ( Guo et al., 2025 ) maintains entity and relation keyword indices; and PathRAG ( Chen et al., 2025 ) prunes relational paths. A
second group varies what is indexed: hyperedges for n n -ary facts ( Luo et al., 2025 ) ,
hierarchical aggregation ( Huang et al., 2025 ) ,
token-efficient construction ( Xiao et al., 2025 ) , separate
similarity and relatedness indices ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) ,
context-dependent structure ( Lau et al., 2026 ) , and
path tracking ( Li et al., 2025 ) . In each
case retrieval is designed together with the structure its own indexing step
produces. The hierarchical lexical graph ( Ghassel et al., 2025 ) makes this
coupling explicit: its retrievers address the statement, fact, topic, and
chunk node types of its own graph model directly in their graph queries.
Some works do vary construction: KGP ( Wang et al., 2023 ) compares several
passage-similarity graphs, HippoRAG ablates its extractor, and Han et al. (2026) find GraphRAG performance stable across the
LLMs used for construction. Studies that compare constructions directly hold
a simple retriever fixed in order to judge the graphs ( da Cruz et al., 2025 ) , or recombine fixed retrieval operators with
different graph types to find the best pairing ( Zhou et al., 2026 ) . In
each case the graph is the object of study and the retriever an instrument;
whether a system transfers across constructions that differ in schema
commitment, typing, and provenance is not tested.
Surveys characterize when graph structure helps over flat retrieval ( Xiang et al., 2026 ) . Table 1 summarizes these differences.

Closest to our setting is work that answers questions over graphs not seen
during development. BYOKG ( Agarwal et al., 2024a ) explores an unseen
graph once to generate query–program exemplars that ground later program
synthesis; SymKGQA ( Agarwal et al., 2024b ) generates step-by-step
symbolic programs from few-shot examples and grounds them with a
retrieval-based resolver; and text-to-Cypher work ( Ozsoy et al., 2024 ) translates
questions into graph queries given a schema.
GRA ( Dragic et al., 2026 ) navigates a hybrid knowledge graph with generic
tools and discovers everything domain-specific at run time, but is evaluated
on a single graph.
The most similar system,
BYOKG-RAG ( Mavromatis et al., 2025 ) , generates
entities, relation paths, and OpenCypher queries over custom graphs and
refines them against retrieved context. It makes no construction assumptions,
but its retrievers presuppose the conventions of curated KGs: relation
semantics carried by edge types listed in a global schema, nodes addressed
by name, and meaningful edge direction. Graphs whose relations are
open-vocabulary strings stored as edge properties, as in our
open-information-extraction constructions, violate these conventions
: their schema exposes a single relationship type, so retrievers that select
among types have nothing to select. This is the setting a query-local
interface is designed for. These systems are
also evaluated as KGQA over curated benchmark graphs (Freebase-based GrailQA
and MetaQA for BYOKG; encyclopedic, temporal, and medical KGs for BYOKG-RAG),
where answers are graph entities; none evaluates multiple constructions of
the same corpus.They establish that LLMs can synthesize executable programs over graphs they
were not built for, and ArcRAG builds on that; our Direct-Cypher agent
(§ 5 ) represents this approach under our setup.

schema suited to encyclopedic text. The extraction-and-commit reflection
loop is otherwise the same loop used for the financial 10-K graph. The
resulting graphs have typed nodes and a closed relation set.

blocks.en: 4 Methodology
blocks.zh: 4 方法

blocks.en:
Real-world knowledge graphs are incomplete and noisy ( Paulheim, 2017 ) : one entity is stored under several names, one
relation as several predicate strings, and edges a question needs may be
missing; open information extraction leaves entity and relation phrases
uncanonicalized altogether ( Vashishth et al., 2018 ) . A retriever written
against one construction’s schema inherits its assumptions about all three.
ArcRAG’s stages can instead be read through the exploration exploitation
trade-off familiar from search ( Kocsis and Szepesvári, 2006 ) , although no
stage implements a bandit or tree-search policy. The Explorer explores: it establishes what the graph
contains around the entities a question names, including their variants,
without committing to an answer. The Planner and Generator exploit: they
commit to the most promising explored paths and execute them as queries.
When the evidence does not support an answer, the search returns to
exploration. The budgets reflect the same trade-off: retries extend exploitation and
passes renew exploration, and how much the Planner’s guidance adds depends
on both the budget and the graph (Appendix D ).

reached. More passes raise accuracy in every ablated configuration

blocks.en: 5.1 Datasets and Samples

blocks.en:
We evaluate on three QA benchmarks that differ in how much composition an
answer requires. MuSiQue ( Trivedi et al., 2022 ) chains up to four single-hop questions, with the bridging entities absent

For RQ1, query-local exploration improves on direct Cypher generation at

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
This is an early study of cross-construction portability, and its scope
reflects that. We evaluate two graph families over the same three corpora,
chosen to differ in kind rather than degree: schema-guided extraction with
typed nodes, a closed relation set, and chunk provenance, against open
information extraction with untyped nodes, free-text relations, and no
provenance. Two maximally different constructions test portability more
severely than several similar ones would, but they do not establish transfer
to curated ontologies or to graphs with different node granularities.
blocks.zh:
这是对跨建筑可移植性及其范围的早期研究
反映这一点。 我们评估两个图表家庭 在同一三只蝎子,
选取的是不同种类而非不同程度的:
键入节点、 闭合关系集和块出处, 对开
信息提取方式为无类型节点、自由文本关系和无
来源。 两个最大的不同构造 测试可移植性更多
比几个相似的都严重 但他们没有确定转移
或用不同节点颗粒的图表。

blocks.en:
Because the two families differ in both structure and provenance, the
accuracy gap between them reflects both, and we do not separate the two.
Canonicalization at query time is a design property of the harness; we do
not measure how much noise or variation it absorbs. Comparisons with prior
GraphRAG systems use their best reported figures, whose protocols and answer
models differ from ours, rather than reruns under a shared setup. Each
configuration is run once, and the answer model samples at temperature 1.0
and also judges whether its own evidence is sufficient, so the results carry
run-to-run variance that we do not quantify.

由于两个家庭在结构和来源上都不同,
它们之间的准确性差距反映了两者,我们没有将两者分开。

没有测量它吸收了多少噪音或变化。 与上一个比较

并判断它本身的证据是否充分,所以结果随同
未量化的从运行到运行的差异。

blocks.en:
The benchmarks are public and the answer model is a large pretrained model,
so parametric knowledge may contribute to absolute scores; comparisons that
share the answer model limit but do not remove this effect. Our experiments
use encyclopedic QA and do not establish reliability for the regulated
domains that motivate traceable retrieval: an executable witness does not
guarantee factual correctness, and deployment there would require
domain-specific validation and human oversight.

context, answer the original query, and self-judge sufficiency. • Stop once the answer is judged sufficient, or the proposed
follow-up query is empty; otherwise re-run on the follow-up query,
accumulating context across passes.

relationship type, almost any query pattern is valid, so refinement becomes

blocks.en:
Figure 3 visualizes the six passes. In Pass 1 , the system resolves Greenwood Laboratory School to Springfield, Missouri ,
successfully identifying the city but leaving the film’s screenwriter
unknown. Since only part of the reasoning chain is resolved, answer
synthesis marks the pass as insufficient.

blocks.en:
In Pass 2 , the planner broadens the search from a precise
entity lookup to a wider search over film credits, retrieving six
candidate screenwriters. Although additional evidence is obtained, none
can yet be confirmed as the correct writer.

候选编剧. 虽然获得了额外证据,但没有
还可以确认为正确的作者。

blocks.en:
In Pass 3 , the search narrows again by investigating the
birthplaces of the candidate set. This eliminates several false leads
and identifies the actual credited writers—Margaret Mayo,
Z. Wall Covington, and Gardner Hunting—but their birthplaces remain

In Pass 4 , the planner further narrows the search to the
birth states of these three writers. Margaret Mayo is found to have

evidence. This partially resolves the reasoning chain but creates a
conflict with the earlier Missouri anchor.

In Pass 5 , the system performs its most targeted search,

blocks.en:
Finally, in Pass 6 , the planner broadens the search once
more, abandoning the exhausted candidate-specific searches and instead
querying whether Springfield served as the capital of any state.
Combining this with the Illinois evidence from Margaret Mayo, the system
retrieves that Springfield, Illinois became the state capital in
1839 , completing the reasoning chain and producing a sufficient answer.

This example demonstrates the iterative search strategy illustrated in
Figure 3 . Rather than repeatedly attempting
the same retrievals, each pass contributes partial progress by
either discovering new entities, eliminating incorrect hypotheses, or
adapting the search scope from precise entity-level retrieval to broader
graph exploration. Evidence accumulates across passes and incrementally
refines the active reasoning chain until the sixth pass has sufficient
evidence to answer the question.

blocks.en: Appendix F Compute and Reproducibility
blocks.zh: 附录F 计算和复制

blocks.en:
All language models and the embedder were accessed through an
OpenAI-compatible inference API; no models were trained or fine-tuned, and
no local GPUs were used. The pipeline is implemented in Python using the
OpenAI client library for model calls, the Neo4j Python driver for Cypher
queries over Memgraph via the Bolt protocol, and the Qdrant client for
hybrid dense and BM25 retrieval ([versions]). The six main runs (three
datasets, two graph families, 1,000 questions each) persist 85.78M tokens
(Appendix C ), and the component ablations comprise 54 runs
over the same 100-question sample. All settings are listed in
Appendix B.2 ; agents run near-greedy (temperature
0.0–0.2), the answer model runs at temperature 1.0, and each configuration
was run once.
